title: Only 6% Of Adults Can Pass This Barrister Entrance Exam
summary: Explore Courtroom Foundations, Cases and Questions, Legal Reasoning, Evidence in Focus, Professional Judgment across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Can you follow the evidence?
Make your strongest case.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: Courtroom Foundations, Cases and Questions, Legal Reasoning, Evidence in Focus, Professional Judgment. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. This is not a bar admission exam, legal qualification or legal advice. Laws and professional rules vary by jurisdiction.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

insights.overview: Your courtroom score at a glance

barrister-q1.question: In a criminal trial, who normally bears the burden of proving the charge?

answers.a1: The prosecution

barrister-q2.question: Which principle treats an accused person as innocent unless guilt is proved?

answers.a1: Strict liability

barrister-round1-new1.question: What is the main role of an advocate in court?

answers.a1: Presenting a client's case within professional duties
answers.a4: Writing the law for the legislature

answers.a1: A claim that has not necessarily been proved

barrister-round1-new3.question: What distinguishes a fact from an inference?

answers.a1: A fact is established information; an inference is a conclusion drawn from information
answers.a2: They always mean exactly the same thing
answers.a4: A fact must be a prediction

barrister-round1-new4.question: What does a court judgment normally set out?

answers.a1: The court's decision and reasoning

barrister-q3.question: What is an earlier court decision that may guide a later similar case called?

answers.a1: An affidavit

barrister-q4.question: What is the questioning of a witness by the opposing side commonly called?

answers.a1: Direct examination

barrister-round2-new1.question: In common-law reasoning, what does distinguishing a precedent mean?

answers.a1: Explaining why material differences make it inapplicable
answers.a2: Pretending the earlier case does not exist

answers.a1: A law enacted by a legislature

barrister-round2-new3.question: Which question is most clearly open-ended?

answers.a1: What did you observe when you arrived?
answers.a3: You saw him leave, didn't you?
answers.a4: Did the alarm sound at nine?

barrister-round2-new4.question: Why distinguish what a witness saw from what they later heard?

answers.a1: The sources and reliability of the information differ
answers.a4: It removes the need to evaluate evidence

barrister-q5.question: What Latin term describes the legal reason essential to a court’s decision?

answers.a1: Ratio decidendi

barrister-q6.question: What is a judicial observation that is not essential to the decision often called?

answers.a1: A binding order
In good faith
At first sight or on initial appearance

barrister-round3-new3.question: Why examine whether two cases share material facts?

answers.a1: To assess the relevance of the earlier reasoning
answers.a2: To ensure both parties have the same names

barrister-round3-new4.question: A rule has an express exception. What should careful analysis do?

answers.a1: Check whether the exception applies
answers.a3: Assume the exception applies to everyone

barrister-q7.question: What term commonly describes an out-of-court statement offered to prove the truth of what it says?

answers.a1: Privilege

barrister-q8.question: Which question most clearly suggests the answer the examiner wants?

answers.a1: What happened next?
answers.a4: The light was red when you crossed, wasn’t it?

barrister-round4-new1.question: Two witnesses give conflicting times. What is the careful response?

answers.a1: Examine their sources and other available evidence
answers.a2: Assume the first witness is right
answers.a3: Average the times and call it proved

answers.a1: Additional evidence supporting an account

barrister-round4-new3.question: Why preserve an original document when possible?

answers.a1: To help assess authenticity and context
answers.a2: Because copies can never be read
answers.a3: To guarantee every statement is true

barrister-round4-new4.question: A quoted sentence is ambiguous without its surrounding paragraph. What should an advocate do?

answers.a1: Consider the relevant context

barrister-q9.question: In public law, what does judicial review primarily assess?

answers.a1: Whether a public decision was made lawfully
answers.a2: Whether a jury chose the best witness
answers.a3: Whether a contract made a profit
answers.a4: Whether every appeal should be allowed

barrister-q10.question: Where the cab-rank rule applies, what does it broadly require of a barrister covered by it, subject to professional rules and exceptions?

answers.a1: Accept only popular cases
answers.a2: Accept suitable instructions regardless of the client’s identity or the case’s popularity

barrister-round5-new1.question: What is a conflict of interest?

answers.a1: A competing interest that may impair professional duties

barrister-round5-new2.question: What should a lawyer do on discovering a material error in their own submission?

answers.a1: Address it through the proper professional and court process
answers.a2: Conceal it because it is inconvenient

barrister-round5-new3.question: Why explain the limits of legal advice across jurisdictions?

answers.a1: Laws and professional rules may differ

barrister-round5-new4.question: Which approach best supports a reasoned legal conclusion?

answers.a1: Link the relevant rule to established facts and consider counterarguments
answers.a3: Rely only on a party's confidence
